key_insight: A hybrid reduced-order plus neural-operator framework can accelerate CFD-like thermal-hydraulic prediction for SMR digital twins while preserving key flow dynamics in a helical coil steam generator.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster transient simulation for reactor monitoring and decision support, with model choice guided by whether the target is instantaneous vortex-resolved fields or mean-flow/pressure-drop estimation.
method: ROM + DeepONet on unstructured mesh data using an MLP autoencoder to form L-DeepONet
ROM + DeepONet on structured mesh data using a convolutional autoencoder to form L-DeepONet
Fourier neural operator (FNO) and multi-scale variants for comparison and spectral-bias mitigation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the multi-scale L-DeepONet captured instantaneous periodic vortex dynamics in velocity and pressure, while FNO variants predicted mean flow and pressure drop reliably.
watch_item: Performance depends on CFD data type and target fidelity; operator models may still struggle with fine transient details if training data are limited or the flow regime shifts.
paper_title: Neural Operator-Based Surrogate Model for CFD:Helical Coil Steam Generator in Small Modular Reactor
